summary.text: A 58-year-old man treated from October 26 to October 28, 2020 for snoring during sleep for 8 years, aggravated with apnea for 3 years. He had no chronic heart disease, hypertension, type 2 diabetes or other chronic diseases, and had a history of cervical spondylosis with cervical internal fixation surgery 7 years earlier.

Upper airway CT showed posterior displacement of the soft palate with narrowing of the oropharyngeal sagittal diameters and postoperative cervical spine changes. Overnight polysomnography gave AHI 44.6/h, supine AHI 60.5/h and minimum oxygen saturation 83%, and CPAP titration gave a 90% pressure of 13 cmH_(2)O; he was diagnosed with severe obstructive sleep apnea. Apart from these findings, no other positive physical findings were reported.

Good compliance with the CPAP treatment and significant improvement of subjective symptoms were reported after treatment, and the post-treatment AHI decreased to 11/h; Table 2 lists an AHI after all-night CPAP of 11/h. After leaving the hospital and returning home he used CPAP regularly and has been receiving regular follow-up.

summary.text: A 70-year-old man seen from May 29 to June 1, 2019 with snoring during sleep for 20 years. He had no chronic heart disease, hypertension, type 2 diabetes or other chronic diseases and denied ostealgia or other neurological symptoms.

Upper airway CT showed obvious osteophytes at the anterior edge of the cervical vertebra, compression and protuberation of the posterior pharyngeal wall and narrower sagittal pharyngeal diameters. Laryngoscopy showed a significant bulge of the posterior laryngopharyngeal wall with small papilloma. Polysomnography gave AHI 72.5/h, supine AHI 74.4/h and minimum oxygen saturation 81%, and CPAP titration gave a 90% pressure of 12 cmH_(2)O; he was diagnosed with severe obstructive sleep apnea. Apart from these findings, no other positive physical findings were reported.

Good compliance with the CPAP treatment and significant improvement of subjective symptoms were reported after treatment, and the post-treatment AHI decreased to 8.8/h; Table 2 lists an AHI after all-night CPAP of 8.8/h. After leaving the hospital and returning home he used CPAP regularly and has been receiving regular follow-up.
